I will do it much like last year, with small adjustments for cost and for the water I can use from the well. I have 8 mu, and my main food-and-cash balance is still wheat-maize on 5 mu and cotton on 3 mu. I do not like changing too much at my age unless I see it working nearby. Around here, if wheat or maize is short of fertilizer, the yield loss hurts more than spending a bit extra, so I would rather feed the crop steadily and not let it go hungry. For wheat, I will keep a fairly solid base fertilizer and give water at the key times, because irrigated wheat in our area can still give good grain if I do not save too hard on nitrogen. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, keep the fertilizer a little stronger, and do simple field work so I do not waste labor, since some family members work off-farm. For cotton, I will not plant too much, only 3 mu, because it needs more watching and more sprays, but I still keep some because cash income matters. I will follow what has worked on my own land and what the better growers nearby are doing: steady fertilizer, enough water, not too fancy, and no cutting corners at the important stages.
